Program structure

Three levels, one learning pathway.

The curriculum moves from undergraduate foundations toward independent research and graduate specialization. The source presentation frames the journey through four connected stages.

Original presentation framing: Opening: Department of Biology curriculum overview · Explain the whole program before details.
01

Bachelor’s

Build language, science, chemistry, physics, taxonomy, ecology, genetics, physiology, innovation, and research skills.

02

Specialization

Elective choices and the year-four project/thesis connect classroom learning to biological questions.

03

Master’s

Students enter pure research or coursework plus research, supported by seminars and thesis work.

04

PhD

Doctoral study emphasizes high-level dissertation research and publishable scientific contribution.

Bachelor’s degree · academic track

Four years of progressive training.

Updated BSc structure: Bachelor of Science Program in Biology, Faculty of Science, two-semester system. The presentation identifies 129 credits and follows the curriculum from broad foundations to independent work.

Year 1 · Semester 28 courses · 20 credits · organic chemistry, zoology, physics

Bachelor’s curriculum · synthesis

Knowledge becomes research capability.

The original presentation recommends explaining the undergraduate curriculum through linked focus areas rather than dozens of isolated course names.

Speaking framework: Explain the undergraduate curriculum through five linked focus areas rather than dozens of separate course names. Five focus areas make the BSc easy to explain.

BSc synthesis

BSc Biology · 4-year academic track

Five focus areas make the bachelor pathway easy to explain while keeping the capstone routes visible.

BSc Biology4-year academic track

Use this slide to summarize bachelor learning without reading all course codes.

General education + basic science

Year 1

Year 1 includes language, general education, introductory chemistry and lab, botany, zoology, physics and lab.

Cell · ecology · genetics

Year 2

Year 2 introduces cell biology, taxonomy, ecology, biodiversity and phylogenetics, genetics, microbiology, and quantitative analysis.

Statistics · physiology · instruments

Year 3

Year 3 emphasizes biostatistics, physiology, instrumentation, biochemistry, biobusiness, and research presentation.

Innovation · project · seminar

Year 3–4

Integrative Biology and Innovation plus electives help students choose a direction.

Thesis / cooperative / international

Capstone

Year 4 moves into Biology Project, Seminar, Undergraduate Thesis, Cooperative Education, or International Training.

Master’s and PhD structure

Two routes into graduate research.

Graduate study is organized by research intensity: a pure research route, or a coursework route that combines advanced subjects with thesis/dissertation work.

Source framing: Graduate structure: route + program + output · Graduate research: MSc + PhD.
A1

Pure Research Track

Research dominates from the beginning.

  • Master’s: Plan A1
  • PhD: Type 1.1
  • Thesis/dissertation credits + mandatory graduate seminars
A2

Coursework + Research

Advanced subjects prepare the research project.

  • Master’s: Plan A2
  • PhD: Type 2.1 / 2.2
  • Core subjects, electives, seminars, and thesis/dissertation

Biological Sciences · visual summary

Core training branches into specialist biology.

Graduate focus areas connect research methodology and seminars to ecology, conservation, plant and animal science, microbiology, molecular biology, and bioinformatics.

Biological Sciences

Biological Sciences · graduate focus

Core: research methodology, advanced biology, and graduate seminars.

Biological SciencesGraduate focus

The program can be introduced as core research training plus elective specializations.

Research methods · seminars

Core training

Core requirements include research methodology, advanced biological science/topics, and graduate seminars.

Advanced ecology · wetlands

Ecology & conservation

Ecology and environmental biology may include conservation biology, environmental biomonitoring, wetland ecology, herpetology, or ornithology.

Physiology · taxonomy · systems

Plant & animal science

Plant and animal science may include advanced plant physiology, plant taxonomy, ultrastructure, animal physiology, evolution and systematics.

Mycology · signaling · bioinformatics

Microbiology & molecular

Microbiology and molecular biology may include applied mycology, cellular signal transduction, applied bioinformatics, and molecular genetics.

Biotechnology · visual summary

Tools flow from genes to processes to impact.

The biotechnology route links advanced methods to molecular engineering, plant tissue and bioinnovation, and environmental or microbial technologies.

Biotechnology

Biotechnology · tools → process → impact

Core: advanced biotechnology, research methodology, and graduate seminar.

BiotechnologyTools → process → impact

Biotechnology links biological mechanisms with practical tools and scalable processes.

Advanced biotech · methodology

Core training

Core requirements include Advanced Biotechnology, Research Methodology in Biotechnology, and Biotechnology Graduate Seminar.

DNA · genomics · proteomics

Molecular engineering

Molecular and genetic engineering can include recombinant DNA technology, applied genomics/proteomics, metabolic engineering, and advanced molecular biology.

Tissue culture · metabolites

Plant tissue & bioinnovation

Plant tissue and bio-innovation can include advanced plant tissue culture, secondary metabolites, bioprocess engineering, and industrial fermentation.

Bioremediation · enzymes

Environmental & microbial tech

Environmental and microbial technology can include bioremediation, waste utilization, microbes in bioindustry, and enzyme technology.

Graduation output requirements

The final product is research.

Graduate study culminates in defensible original research and, depending on program rules, publication or accepted-manuscript requirements.

Source emphasis: Research is the graduate-level output.

Thesis · publications

Master of Science

Students complete and defend an original thesis. The degree output is built around a research project and a publishable contribution.

  • Thesis defense
  • Graduate seminar participation
  • At least one peer-reviewed publication or accepted manuscript, depending on program rules

Dissertation · international output

Doctor of Philosophy

PhD study centers on a high-impact dissertation and publication-quality research contribution.

  • Doctoral dissertation defense
  • Advanced research independence
  • Publications in recognized international databases, depending on program rules

Faculty members · category view

Research strengths across people.

Faculty are grouped by specialization so curriculum focus areas connect directly to mentors—from genetics and diagnostics to plant science, ecology, organismal biology, and biotechnology.

Faculty I: Categories make faculty expertise easier to discuss. Faculty II: From plant science to biotechnology — plant biology, biotechnology, systematics, and physiology. Faculty III: Organismal biology, ecology, and diagnostics — organisms, conservation, vectors, anatomy, and diagnostics.

Core instrumentation

Shared analytical & imaging capabilities.

Department / Faculty research infrastructure. The source package presents 18 systems across chromatography and mass spectrometry, electron microscopy, spectroscopy and elemental analysis, and cell-analysis/lab-support platforms.

Chromatography & mass spectrometry

  • UPLC-QTOF MSUltra-Performance LC + Quadrupole Time-of-Flight MS
  • UPLC-TQ MSUltra-Performance LC + Triple Quadrupole MS
  • GC-MS/MSTriple Quadrupole Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry
  • Preparative HPLCHPLC with automated fraction collector

Electron microscopy

  • FE-SEMField Emission Scanning Electron Microscope
  • TEMTransmission Electron Microscope
  • SEMStandard Scanning Electron Microscope

Spectroscopy & elemental analysis

  • NMRNuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectrometer
  • FT-IRFourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer
  • ICP-OESInductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometer
  • GFAASGraphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometer
  • Horiba DeltaFlexSpectrofluorometer & fluorescence lifetime system
  • FluorometryFluorescence intensity and emission measurements

Cell analysis, screening & lab support

  • XRDX-Ray Diffractometer
  • TGA / DSCThermogravimetric Analyzer / Differential Scanning Calorimeter
  • BioTek Synergy H1Multi-Mode Microplate Reader
  • Flow CytometrySingle-cell fluorescence and population analysis
  • Merck Milli-Q Integral 3High-Purity Water System

Collaboration opportunity

Invitation for MOU Collaboration.

A practical framework for joint graduate education, research, mobility & shared infrastructure.

01

Joint Graduate Tracks

Collaborative split-site and co-advised M.Sc. / Ph.D. programs using our zero-coursework research tracks.

02

High-Impact Publishing

Co-authoring joint research targeted at top-tier Scopus (Q1/Q2) and Web of Science journals.

03

Talent Mobility

Reciprocal exchange pipelines for student internships, credit-transfers, and faculty sabbaticals.

04

Shared Infrastructure

Open access to advanced equipment: NGS, HPC Supercomputer, UPLC-QTOF, and FE-SEM.

05

Regional Field Access

Direct collaboration on tropical biodiversity and conservation through our Research Center for Excellence in Biodiversity.

06

Fast-Track Administration

Streamlined institutional processing for visa coordination, matching grants, and agreements.

Proposed outcome: a focused MOU that turns shared strengths into joint degrees, publications, mobility and research access.

Department in context

Campus & student learning.

The working package also includes department/campus and student-activity photography. These are retained here as supporting visual material.

Department of Biology is part of the Faculty of Science at Naresuan University in Phitsanulok, Thailand. The department supports biology education from bachelor’s foundations to graduate research and specialist biological contribution.
